report:
## Conclusion: No—the best evidence does not support sustained benefit over placebo.

High-quality research indicates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) does **not meaningfully improve benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) urinary symptoms in the longer term**. The 2023 Cochrane review found little to no clinically important benefit versus placebo, including at follow-ups of **12–17 months**, for urinary symptoms, quality of life, nocturia, and urinary flow.  
https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD001423.pub4/full  
https://www.aafp.org/afp/2024/0500/cochrane-saw-palmetto-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia

Two especially important placebo-controlled trials support that conclusion:

- **STEP:** 225 men with moderate-to-severe BPH took 160 mg twice daily for one year; saw palmetto did not improve symptoms or urinary-flow measures more than placebo.  
  https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa053085

- **CAMUS:** 369 men received escalating doses—up to triple the usual dose—over 72 weeks. Even 960 mg/day did not reduce lower urinary tract symptoms more than placebo.  
  https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/1104439

Earlier small or lower-quality studies sometimes suggested modest improvement, but larger, longer, better-controlled trials and successive Cochrane reviews have not confirmed those findings. Saw palmetto appears generally well tolerated, but the evidence does not justify expecting meaningful long-term symptom relief compared with placebo.
